# AnatomyOf

> An interactive, annotated tour of what's inside a source file, one language at a time. Hover a callout to trace it into the code; click it for an in-depth writeup.

AnatomyOf opens an example source file in a code window with color-coded callouts explaining every structural part: shebang, imports, class definitions, control flow, and more. Every language ships a minimal and a verbose example, light and dark themes, and shareable URLs like `/#/python/verbose`. Beyond real languages, concept pages dissect the structural anatomy of a website, a settings screen, a mobile app, a dashboard, an email, a CI pipeline, and a GitHub contribution: the same idea, applied to things that aren't code.

## Key facts
- Dozens of languages, plus concept pages: from Python and Rust to Ada, Prolog, COBOL, GML, and WebAssembly.
- Color-coded callouts wired to the exact lines they describe.
- Hover to trace, click to dive: a full deep-dive modal per concept, with a Learn more link.
- Light and dark themes, and fully mobile-responsive (tap to pin a callout, tap again to open it).
- Sidebar ranked by real-world popularity (TIOBE Index), toggleable to A-Z, with instant search.
- Syntax highlighting by Shiki, the same engine VS Code uses.
- Deep-linkable URLs for every language and variant.
- Built with Bun, Vite, Vue 3, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS 4, Reka UI, Shiki, and Biome.
- Free and open source under the MIT License.
- Privacy: one anonymous visit ping per page load to LunarWerx's own endpoint, no cookies, no third-party trackers, no personal data; Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are honored.

## Common questions

### Is AnatomyOf free?
Yes. AnatomyOf is free and open source under the MIT License, with the full source published on GitHub. There is no account, no trial, and no paid tier: opening the site is the whole of getting started.

### Which languages does it cover?
Dozens, ranging from mainstream ones like Python and Rust to Ada, Prolog, COBOL, GML, and WebAssembly. Alongside the real languages, concept pages dissect the structural anatomy of a website, a settings screen, a mobile app, a dashboard, an email, a CI pipeline, and a GitHub contribution.

### Does AnatomyOf track me?
No. It sends one anonymous visit ping per page load to LunarWerx's own endpoint. There are no cookies, no third-party trackers, and no personal data of any kind. Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control are both honored.

### Can I link someone straight to one language?
Yes. Every language and variant has its own deep-linkable URL, in the shape `/#/python/verbose`, so a link opens exactly the file and the verbosity level you were looking at rather than the front page.

### Does it work on a phone?
Yes. The layout is fully mobile-responsive, and the callouts adapt to touch: tap a callout to pin it against the code, then tap it again to open its full deep-dive writeup.
